previous_description: Specifies data validation constraints for FieldAccessControl, defining allowed patterns, value ranges, or transformations applied when accessing protected fields. Prevents data corruption and enforces field-level integrity.
definition: A single input-validation constraint (regex pattern, numeric range, length limit, allowed-value list or custom check) that the value of a protected field or request attribute must satisfy, with a violation message and severity. It accepts or rejects the value itself and does not decide who may access it.

distinguish_from.when: the predicate tests a request-context attribute (user, role, time, IP) to decide whether the request is authorized, rather than checking that a supplied value is well-formed.
the concern is how a field's value is masked, redacted or hidden from unauthorized principals, rather than which values are acceptable.
the unit produces a permit/deny decision with optional obligations, rather than a pass/fail check with a violation message.
the constraints are the complete credential complexity, rotation and lockout regime, rather than one individual check that such a policy might use.

standard_reference: NIST SP 800-53 SI-10 Information Input Validation
code_evidence: Bean Validation, Pydantic, Joi or Zod constraints such as @Pattern, @Size, constr(regex=...) or .max() declared on security-sensitive DTO fields like email, account number, token or redirect URL.
Input-sanitization middleware or allowlist regexes that reject a request with HTTP 400/422 and a specific error message when a parameter fails the check.

A validator function or schema entry named for the check (e.g. validateIban, SAFE_FILENAME_RE) referenced from an access-control or field-protection layer, with configurable severity or logging on failure.
notes: The definition mentions 'transformations', but no enum value or attribute models a transformation; remove the word or add one. The 'length' type allows only a maximum, so a minimum length cannot be expressed. No attribute names the target field, so the target is implied only by relationships. Boundary with data-model schema constraints needs a rule: model only security-motivated validation here.
